root_cause.text: In `arch/x86/platform/efi/quirks.c`, EFI boot services memory was being released too early with `memblock_free_late()` from `efi_free_boot_services()`, so under `CONFIG_DEFERRED_STRUCT_PAGE_INIT` the freed pages could still be in uninitialized `struct page` regions and therefore were skipped by `memblock_free_pages()`, leaking RAM instead of actually freeing it.
root_cause.evidence: The patch notes that `efi_free_boot_services()` “frees memory occupied by EFI_BOOT_SERVICES_CODE and EFI_BOOT_SERVICES_DATA using memblock_free_late()”, and explicitly says that when the memory map is still uninitialized “they won't be actually freed because memblock_free_late() calls memblock_free_pages() and the latter skips uninitialized pages”; the fix splits this into `efi_unmap_boot_services()` plus a later `arch_initcall(efi_free_boot_services)` that uses `free_reserved_area()` after deferred init completes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Rename the EFI boot-services cleanup API to more accurately reflect that it unmaps boot services.
intent_record.what: In the EFI header declarations, the external function prototype `efi_free_boot_services(void)` was renamed to `efi_unmap_boot_services(void)`; no other code in this hunk changed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes the symbol name expected by callers from a function implying release of boot services to one implying unmapping of boot services, which likely reflects a different or more accurate teardown action while preserving the same call site interface shape.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace freeing EFI boot services with unmapping them during virtual mode entry to correct boot services teardown behavior.
intent_record.what: In `__efi_enter_virtual_mode()`, the call to `efi_free_boot_services()` was replaced with `efi_unmap_boot_services()` after `efi_check_for_embedded_firmwares()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, EFI boot services are no longer freed at this point; instead, their mappings are unmapped. This changes the transition into virtual mode so the code preserves the underlying boot services memory while removing its accessible mappings, which affects how subsequent EFI runtime setup interacts with that memory.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the comment to match the actual boot-services memory release path.
intent_record.what: A comment in efi_reserve_boot_services() was updated: the text now says the memblock_reserve() for this region is paired with free_reserved_area() in efi_free_boot_services() instead of memblock_free_late().
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime behavior; it only corrects the documentation in the source to reflect the actual freeing function used for that reserved region.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add tracking storage and allocation failure handling for EFI boot-service memory unmapping.
intent_record.what: The function `efi_free_boot_services()` was renamed to `efi_unmap_boot_services()`. A new `struct efi_freeable_range` with `start` and `end` fields was added, along with a new static pointer `ranges_to_free`. Inside the function, new local variables `idx` and `sz` were introduced. Before iterating EFI memory descriptors, the code now allocates zeroed storage for `ranges_to_free` using `kzalloc()`, logs an error and returns if allocation fails, and computes the allocation size from `efi.memmap.nr_map` plus 1.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now prepares an auxiliary array to record EFI memory ranges that can be freed later, instead of immediately proceeding without that bookkeeping. This adds a dependency on successful allocation of range-tracking storage; if allocation fails, boot-services unmapping stops early and an error is reported. The change likely supports later unmapping/freeing logic by preserving the set of reclaimable EFI regions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Defer EFI boot-service memory freeing until deferred page initialization has completed to avoid freeing uninitialized memory too early.
intent_record.what: The call to `memblock_free_late(start, size);` was removed inside `efi_free_boot_services()`. In its place, the code now stores each range into `ranges_to_free[idx].start` and `ranges_to_free[idx].end`, increments `idx`, and adds a comment explaining that with `CONFIG_DEFERRED_STRUCT_PAGE_INIT` the memory cannot be reliably freed at this point and must be queued for later.
intent_record.how: Instead of immediately freeing EFI boot service memory, the function now defers freeing those ranges until a later stage when memory structures are fully initialized. This prevents attempting to release memory prematurely when some struct page state is still unavailable or incomplete.

intent_record.intent_summary: Automatically free reserved EFI boot services memory during early boot and report the reclaimed space.
intent_record.what: The code adds a new static __init function named efi_free_boot_services() that iterates over ranges_to_free, converts each physical range start/end to virtual addresses, calls free_reserved_area() on each range, accumulates the total freed size, frees the ranges_to_free array with kfree(), and logs the amount freed. It also registers this function with arch_initcall(efi_free_boot_services).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the kernel will now automatically release EFI boot services memory ranges early in boot, instead of leaving them reserved indefinitely, which increases usable memory and cleans up the temporary range list after use.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the comment to refer to efi_unmap_boot_services() instead of the old boot-services API name.
intent_record.what: The comment in the function documentation was updated to replace "efi_free_boot_services()" with "efi_unmap_boot_services()" in the note about when the routine must be called.
intent_record.how: This changes no runtime behavior; it only corrects the referenced API name in the documentation to reflect the proper boot-services teardown step.

grouping_result.intent: Rename the EFI boot-services cleanup API to more accurately reflect that it unmaps boot services.
Add tracking storage and allocation failure handling for EFI boot-service memory unmapping.
Update the comment to refer to efi_unmap_boot_services() instead of the old boot-services API name.
Defer EFI boot-service memory freeing until deferred page initialization has completed to avoid freeing uninitialized memory too early.
Automatically free reserved EFI boot services memory during early boot and report the reclaimed space.

consistency_review.core_intent: Improve EFI boot-services teardown by tracking boot-service memory so it can be unmapped correctly during virtual mode entry, including allocation failure handling.
Update boot-services comments so they refer to the correct memory release path/API name.

relevance_review.reason: The change only renames the EFI boot-services cleanup API and does not alter the memory-freeing logic in efi_free_boot_services() or address the deferred struct page init leak caused by memblock_free_late().

The group changes EFI boot-services teardown behavior in the same area as the root cause. It replaces early freeing with tracking/unmapping during virtual mode entry, which directly addresses the bug where boot-services memory was released too soon and could be skipped by memblock_free_pages under CONFIG_DEFERRED_STRUCT_PAGE_INIT.
The changes only update comments and API references, without altering the boot-services memory release behavior that caused the leaked RAM.

The group directly addresses the reported bug: EFI boot-services memory was freed too early with memblock_free_late(), and the change defers freeing until deferred struct page initialization is complete, which matches the root cause.

The group concerns automatically freeing EFI boot services memory during early boot, which is the same area as the root cause. Since the vulnerability is about that memory being released too early and not actually freed under CONFIG_DEFERRED_STRUCT_PAGE_INIT, this change is directly related.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct early-freeing call in efi_free_boot_services(); under CONFIG_DEFERRED_STRUCT_PAGE_INIT it can release EFI boot-service pages before their struct page entries are initialized, causing memblock_free_pages() to skip them and leak RAM.
This function is the site where EFI boot-service memory was freed too early; the vulnerability stems from its implementation using early memblock freeing instead of deferring until safe.
This call triggers the buggy boot-services teardown path, leading into the premature freeing behavior that leaked RAM when deferred struct page initialization was enabled.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the premature EFI boot-services memory release. Under CONFIG_DEFERRED_STRUCT_PAGE_INIT, freeing with memblock_free_late() can occur before the corresponding struct page entries are initialized, so memblock_free_pages() later skips those pages and RAM is leaked instead of being freed.
